title: Hebrew calendar with the 17th and 27th of Cheshvan circled
summary: A full Hebrew calendar of twelve numbered months (Tishri to Elul) laid out in three columns, with the feasts Sukkot, Chanukkah, Pesach (Passover) and Shavuot marked. In month 2, Cheshvan, the 17th is circled in yellow and the 27th in dark olive, matching the colours of the flood dates in Genesis 7:11 and 8:14.

text.text: 1 Tishri: days 1–30; SUKKOT marked on 15–22 (19 20 21 22 in green)
2 Cheshvan: days 1–29; the 17th circled in yellow and the 27th circled in dark olive
3 Kislev: days 1–30; Chanukkah marked at the end of the month, ending on 30
7 Nisan: days 1–30; PESACH PASSOVER marked from 14 to 22 (in red)
9 Sivan: days 3–30; 6 and 7 in gold, SHAVUOT marked

numbers.note: numbered months of the Hebrew year, Tishri (1) to Elul (12)
17th of Cheshvan (month 2), circled in yellow: the day the flood began (Genesis 7:11)
27th of Cheshvan (month 2), circled in dark olive: the day the earth was dry (Genesis 8:14)

uncertain: Exact day ranges of the feast labels (SUKKOT, PESACH PASSOVER, SHAVUOT, Chanukkah) are approximate because the words are spread across the day numbers
Day 20 of Cheshvan is partly hidden by the olive circle
